main_body: Sandy ground patch (terrain tiles, 64x48 area shown as a flat sand surface with scattered tan and brown speckles and a small grey stone and a red cross mark)

evidence: The candidate is a flat ground patch of sand with speckle variation. It is terrain, not a standing object, so the 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply. No elevation, side face or slab is drawn. Nothing in it breaks the terrain kind.

style.evidence: The sand uses a base tone plus lighter and darker tan speckles, giving about 3 distinct steps. The reference grass and paving have 5-6 steps with clumps, per-stone shading and darker tufts. The candidate's speckles are sparse, single-pixel or 2-pixel dots on a mostly flat base, so large areas read as one colour. The scattered grey stone and red cross are isolated accents rather than integrated texture. Tiles carry roughly 3-5 colours, well below the reference's median of about 10. It reads thinner and flatter than the reference.
